sections.title: Quantum Engineering
sections.description: Quantum engineering - the design, fabrication, and control of quantum coherent devices - has emerged as a multidisciplinary field spanning physics, electrical engineering, materials science, chemistry, and biology, with the potential for transformational advances in computation, secure communication, and nanoscale sensing. This course surveys the state of the art in quantum hardware, beginning with an overview of the physical implementation requirements for a quantum computer and proceeding to a synopsis of the leading contenders for quantum building blocks, including spins in semiconductors, superconducting circuits, photons, and atoms. The course combines background material on the fundamental physics and engineering principles required to build and control these devices with readings drawn from the current literature, including promising architectures for scaling physical qubits into larger devices and secure communication networks, and for nanoscale sensing applications impacting biology, chemistry, and materials science.

sections.title: Quantum Engineering
sections.description:
Quantum engineering has emerged as a transdisciplinary field spanning physics, electrical engineering, computer science, materials science, chemistry, and biology. It has the potential for transformational advances in computation, secure communication, and nanoscale sensing. This course surveys the state of the art in quantum hardware, beginning with an overview of the physical implementation requirements for a quantum computer and proceeding to a discussion of well-established quantum building blocks, including spins in semiconductors, superconducting circuits, photons, and atoms. The course combines background material on the fundamental physics and engineering principles required to build and control these devices with readings drawn from the current literature, surveying promising architectures for quantum computers, quantum sensors, and quantum communication networks.
Topics covered:
• History of quantum computing and generalized requirements.
• Quantum dynamics, coherent control, decoherence, and measurements.
• Survey of qubit realizations: photons, spins, atoms, and superconducting circuits.
• Fundamentals of quantum computing, quantum communication, and quantum sensing.
• Scalable architectures and quantum error correction.
